scenes.vo: In December twenty sixteen, JPMorgan's CEO said a single credit card would cost the bank up to three hundred million dollars.

visual.sub:
WHAT ONE CREDIT CARD
COST THE BANK IN A QUARTER

scenes.vo: The card: Chase Sapphire Reserve. Four hundred fifty dollars a year, launched two months earlier.

visual.sub:
CHASE SAPPHIRE RESERVE
LAUNCHED TWO MONTHS EARLIER

scenes.vo: It came with a three hundred dollar travel credit and fifteen hundred dollars in bonus points.

visual.headline:
A $450 FEE…
THAT NEARLY PAID FOR ITSELF

scenes.vo: Demand was so high, Chase ran out of the metal used to make the card.

visual.sub:
OF THE METAL USED
TO MAKE THE CARD

scenes.vo: JPMorgan's CEO later said he wished the card had cost the bank even more.

visual.quote: “I wish it cost more … now we have to account for acquisition cost in that business.”
visual.who: Jamie Dimon, JPMorgan CEO · CNBC, Jan 2017

scenes.vo: The next year, the signup bonus was cut in half, down to fifty thousand points.

visual.sub:
THE BONUS WAS CUT
IN HALF THE FOLLOWING YEAR

scenes.vo: When a deal is good enough to go viral, the company pays for it.

visual.display: When a deal is good enough to go *viral,* the company *pays* for it.
